articles.title: Cyberabad civic body plans ₹169-crore net-zero headquarters on the edge of Kotha Kunta lake
articles.description: The Cyberabad Municipal Corporation has invited tenders for a ₹169-crore twin-tower net-zero green complex at Izzath Nagar to serve as its permanent headquarters.

articles.title: India's MSME registrations cross 10 crore on Udyam platforms
articles.description: India's Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises sector has crossed 10 crore registrations on the Udyam Registration Portal and Udyam Assist Platform (as of the end of October 2026), advancing the country's journey towards building a more formalised, inclusive and digitally empowered MSME sector, an official statement said on Wednesday. The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises said registrations grew from 1.02 crore in 2020 to over 10 crore, reflecting the increasing adoption of digital platforms and the government's sustained commitment to bringing enterprises into the formal economic framework. The Udyam Registration Portal, launched on July 1, 2020, introduced a fully online, paperless and self-declaration-based registration process for enterprises, eliminating the requirement for physical documents or proof uploads. Integration with Aadhaar and PAN-based details, along with GST and Income Tax databases, further streamlined the registration process. The system also eliminated the requirement for renewal and made registration completely free of cost, making formalisation simpler and more accessible for entrepreneurs across the country. Udyam Assist Platform facilitates the formalisation of eligible informal micro-enterprises through a simplified mechanism involving designated financial institutions and other partner agencies. Udyam registration supports the identification of enterprises by banks and financial institutions, facilitating the implementation of initiatives such as the Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE), Priority Sector Lending and other credit and Finance related programmes. Further, formal recognition through Udyam supports the broader objectives of various Government initiatives, including the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), National SC-ST Hub, Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises and other entrepreneurship development programmes, subject to applicable eligibility requirements. Women-led enterprises accounted for 3.76 crore registrations, accounting for 37.8 per cent of all registrations across the Udyam Registration Portal and Udyam Assist Platform.â€"IANSaar/pk

articles.title: India's MSME registrations cross 10 crore on Udyam platforms
articles.description: New Delhi, Nov 25 (IANS) India's Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises sector has crossed 10 crore registrations on the Udyam Registration Portal and Udyam Assist Platform, as of the end of October 2026, advancing the country's journey towards building a more formalised, inclusive and digitally empowered MSME sector, an official statement said on Wednesday. The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises said registrations grew from 1.02 crore in 2020 to over 10 crore, reflecting the increasing adoption of digital platforms and the government's sustained commitment to bringing enterprises into the formal economic framework. The Udyam Registration Portal, launched on July 1, 2020, introduced a fully online, paperless and self-declaration-based registration process for enterprises, eliminating the requirement for physical documents or proof uploads. Integration with Aadhaar and PAN-based details, along with GST and Income Tax databases, further streamlined the registration process. The system also eliminated the requirement for renewal and made registration completely free of cost, making formalisation simpler and more accessible for entrepreneurs across the country. Udyam registration supports the identification of enterprises by banks and financial institutions, facilitating the implementation of initiatives such as the Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE), Priority Sector Lending and other credit and Finance related programmes. articles.title: FPJ Exclusive: How Indian AI Startup Zelmier Is Cutting Government Tender Preparation Time From Hours To Under 10 Minutes
articles.description: In an exclusive interview with FPJ Tech Editor Tasneem Kanchwala, Zelmier founder Pranjal Srivastava reveals how his AI startup is reducing government tender discovery and bid preparation time to eight to nine minutes. The bootstrapped startup tracks 82 government platforms and serves 144 businesses.
